---
title: Source
---

## Overview

A **source** retrieves documents. A **tool** exposes an action to the model. Keeping them separate allows the same Elasticsearch, web, or file source to support search visit, or a custom tool interface.

Built-in sources:

| Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | Full-text search and fetch under a local directory; requires `rg` |
| `elasticsearch` | BM25, vector, or hybrid retrieval from an Elasticsearch index |
| `web` | Serper search and Jina page fetch |
| `custom` | A project-defined `DataSource` implementation |

## Configure sources

Configuration accepts a list of `SourceConfig`. Each source has a unique `name`. Source-backed tools refer to those names to decide with source they search/fetch from:

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: file
      name: docs
      root_path: ./docs

  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search
      source: [docs]
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source: [docs]
```

## Local files

To search from local files, specify root folder path in `root_path`. The `search` tool specified with the source would launch a `ripgrep` full text search within `root_path`. The `visit` tool would fetch the full file specified with file path as `document_id`.

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: file
      name: file
      root_path: /path/to/file/root
```

## Web

To search from web. There should be a SERP API to connect to. For example, [Serper](https://serper.dev/). The `search` tool uses serp api to aquire web search result.

[Jina](https://jina.ai/) is a webpage reader specified in converting webpages to LLM-friendly format. When using the web source, `visit` tool uses Jina to read webpages.

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: web
      name: web_source
      serper_api_key: API_KEY
      jina_api_key: API_KEY
```

## Elasticsearch

To search from a local knowledge base, SearcherKit supports searching from elasticsearch endpoint

### Search Mode

Searching in elasticsearch source supports `vector_search_mode: bm25`, `vector`, or `hybrid`. Vector and hybrid modes require an embedding model endpoint and a populated vector field in the index.

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: elasticsearch
      name: corpus
      hosts: http://127.0.0.1:9200
      index: documents
      search_fields: [title, text]
      document_id_field: url
      fetch_field: url
      vector_search_mode: hybrid
      vector_field: text_vector
      embedding_model: Qwen3-Embedding-8B
      embedding_base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8004/v1
      embedding_api_key: EMPTY
      es_max_concurrency: 256
      embedding_max_concurrency: 256
```

::: {.callout-tip}
To use `vector` and `hybrid` search. You needs an embedding model. To serve the model locally, we recommand using [Text Embeddings Interface](https://github.com/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference)
:::

::: {.callout-caution}
Some embedding models use different prompts between query embedding and indexing embedding generation. For example, `Qwen3-Embedding-8B` have
```{.json filename="config_sentence_transformers.json"}
{
  "prompts": {
    "query": "Instruct: Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query\nQuery:",
    "document": ""
  }
}
```

Check carefully on your embedding API / inference engines on how these configurations are processed.

For our recommanded method, [Text Embeddings Interface](https://github.com/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference) dose not autometically append the prompt to the query, thus, configure the prompt with `embedding_prefix` under source configuration.

```yaml
agent:
  sources:
    - type: elasticsearch
      name: corpus
      embedding_prefix: "Instruct: Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query\nQuery:"
```
:::

### Highlighting
Set `highlight: true` to build compact, search-engine-style snippets from matching fragments. Tune `highlight_fragment_size`, `highlight_number_of_fragments`, and `snippet_chars` to control the returned context.

Search mode should always set to `hybrid` when using highlight.


### Build elasticsearch index

SearcherKit provides plugin to quickly deploy knowledgebase to elasticsearch

Deploy a local Wiki index:

```bash
searchagent plugins deploy local-wiki \
  --wiki_dump_path data/wiki.xml.bz2 \
  --es_host http://127.0.0.1:9200 \
  --index_name wiki_local \
  --overwrite
```

Deploy BrowseComp Plus:

```bash
searchagent plugins deploy browsecomp-plus \
  --dataset_path data/browsecomp_plus_corpus.jsonl \
  --es_host http://127.0.0.1:9200 \
  --index_name browsecomp_plus \
  --overwrite
```

## Configure Tools



## Customize the model-visible tool

Tool behavior and model-facing presentation are configured independently:

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search_web
      description: Search the indexed web corpus for evidence.
      source: [corpus]
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        properties:
          query:
            type: string
            description: A focused search query.
        required: [query]
        additionalProperties: false
      raise_argument_validation_error: false
```

`argument_mapping` can rename model-visible arguments before execution. Keep schemas
small and unambiguous: the model should see only arguments it can use correctly.


The tool name, description, and input
schema are visible to the model.

## Summarize large tool results

Search and visit tools can pass their output through a separate summarizer model:

```yaml
agent:
  tools:
    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source: [corpus]
      summary_goal_key: goal
      summarizer:
        model: Qwen3-8B
        base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1
        api_key: EMPTY
        max_chars: 40000
        max_concurrency: 128
        default_kwargs:
          max_tokens: 1024
        retry_config:
          max_tries: 3
```

The summarizer reduces context growth but adds latency and another failure surface.
Use it when raw documents are substantially larger than the evidence needed.

## MCP tools

Use `type: mcp` to expose a tool hosted by an MCP server. Configure the server
transport and remote tool name in the `ToolConfig` fields used by `MCPTool`. MCP tools
share the same initialization, validation, retry, and shutdown lifecycle as native
tools.

For custom retrieval, subclass `DataSource` and use `type: custom` with a `target`.
For custom model actions, subclass `BaseTool` and register the implementation with
`register_tool()` before building the agent.

For complete examples of defining and configuring these extensions, see
[Custom source](../04-developement/01-development.qmd#custom-source) and
[Custom tool](../04-developement/01-development.qmd#custom-tool) in the
development guide.
